text:
Andrei Kuzmenko's stop in Pittsburgh is his fifth NHL team in five seasons, and it hasn't started well: one assist and no goals in 12 games, at about 12.7 minutes a night and falling. Hockey Hot Stove's Ryan Wilson was blunt on Nov. 9, wondering aloud whether Ville Koivunen was hurt because Kuzmenko doesn't deserve a jersey otherwise.

Some of the slump is luck. He has 1.55 expected goals and nothing to show for it, and the Penguins have scored 4.3 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. But the process isn't great either: Pittsburgh is out-chanced with him at five on five (45%), much worse than without him. He's never been a skater (7th percentile top speed by NHL Edge) and has no power-play points yet. Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits his clean exits. The undrafted winger who scored his way out of the KHL needs the puck in good spots, and a Penguins team hearing this much trade talk may not wait long.
